milestones.title: Measure where the first response time goes
acceptance_criteria: Measured per-stage p50 and p95 exist for the first assistant response
A recorded decision links one lever and a budget to those numbers

milestones.title: Reduce the latency with behaviour pinned
acceptance_criteria: The first-turn behaviour is covered by a no-network test before the change
The reduction meets the budget in a before and after measurement with the suites passing

tasks.title: Build the first-turn latency harness
tasks.objective: A repeatable command sends scripted first-turn conversations to /api/asistente-guiado, joins each request by id with the per-model-round and per-tool ms of the audit log, writes a JSON summary of per-stage p50 and p95 with the flags in force, and offers three checkers (summary-check, decision-check, budget-check) that exit non-zero when a file does not meet its rule
tasks.estimate_rationale: SSE reading and the audit-log schema both exist; the open parts are joining log lines by request id on the real files and defining the three checker rules, which T2, T3 and T6 rely on
acceptance_criteria: The harness prints one timeline per request with first texto and fin offsets in milliseconds
The audit-log join matches model rounds and tools to the request by its id
A recorded SSE transcript parses into the same timeline in a test that needs no network

summary-check fails below the minimum run count, decision-check fails without one allowed lever, a budget strictly below the baseline p50 (equal fails) and a numeric p95 tolerance in percent, and budget-check fails when p50 misses the budget or any stage p95 exceeds its baseline value times one plus that tolerance, each covered by the test

verification.purpose: parse a recorded SSE transcript and a sample audit log into a stage timeline and exercise the three checkers with passing and failing fixtures

complexity.justification: Known pieces to assemble: an SSE reader already exists and the log record shape is documented, so the reasoning is bounded to the join

scope.justification: One new script, its pure-parser test and one npm script entry; no application behaviour is touched

duration.justification: Comparable to the earlier latency-summary work, plus a small parser test and the log join on real files
evidence: command:git -C /home/david/dev/pictures log --oneline -1 0ffe9fe0 -> feat(a0.3) resumen run.json con latencias, formato, flip rate y costo

risk.justification: Read-only tooling that only issues requests and reads logs; a defect would give a wrong number, not a wrong answer for customers

coupling.justification: Only an npm script entry and new files are added, and later tasks consume the command after this one is done

confidence.justification: The SSE reader and the log schema were read; the join against real log lines is not yet exercised

tasks.title: Measure the baseline first-turn latency by stage
tasks.objective: The file eval/latencia-asistente/baseline.json holds p50 and p95 milliseconds for each stage of the first assistant response (rules before the model, each model round, each tool, first streamed text) over at least 10 live runs per scenario, with the thinking level and Python flag in force recorded in it
tasks.estimate_rationale: Live paid model calls: the task depends on available Gemini quota and a running local dev server, and effort is mostly waiting on them; whether the key, the local services and the production logs are reachable and representative is unknown
acceptance_criteria: Each scenario has at least 10 recorded runs with per-stage p50 and p95 in the baseline file
The baseline file states which model path and thinking level were in force for the runs
The stage with the largest share of time to first useful response is named with its number

verification.purpose: the baseline file exists, covers three scenarios and has at least 10 runs each

verification.value: with the owner's approval read the VPS audit log with npm run registros -- conversaciones --origen vps --desde 24h and compare its flags with the local run
verification.purpose: learn whether production uses the same path and thinking level
verification.expected: a note of the production path and thinking level, or that the log was not reachable

complexity.justification: Reading timings across the route, the agent loop and the provider hop to attribute time needs judgement but no new design

scope.justification: Produces a measurement and a table; no repository file changes beyond runtime logs that are not tracked

duration.justification: Local logs hold no assistant turn today, so the baseline must be generated and its duration depends on real model latency
evidence: command:python3 (inline aggregate of data/registros events) -> 4 happie requests and no asistente-guiado turn locally
assumption:the dev server, key and quota are available during the run

risk.justification: A wrong or unrepresentative baseline would misdirect every later task, and the run spends paid calls and may read production logs

coupling.justification: The run consumes the paid provider quota and a local server that T6 reuses, and it needs the harness from T1 finished first

confidence.justification: Production path and thinking level cannot be read from the repository, and network variance of real calls is unknown
evidence: assumption:production flags equal the local ones

tasks.title: Choose the reduction lever and budget from the baseline
tasks.objective: The file eval/latencia-asistente/decision.json names the stage that dominates time to first useful response, the single lever chosen among those the code allows, the rejected levers with their measured reason, a latency budget in milliseconds strictly below the baseline p50, and a p95 tolerance in percent taken from the observed run-to-run spread of the baseline
tasks.estimate_rationale: The decision depends entirely on numbers that do not exist yet; the reasoning spans the route, the agent loop, the Python hop and the prompt
acceptance_criteria: The decision file cites the baseline stage numbers it ranks
Exactly one primary lever is chosen and each rejected lever has a measured reason
The budget is a number strictly below the measured p50 and not a guess
The p95 tolerance is a percentage justified by the run-to-run spread seen in the baseline file
The decision file is committed in the tracked eval folder so it survives branch and worktree isolation

verification.value: npx tsx scripts/eval/medir-latencia-asistente.ts decision-check eval/latencia-asistente/decision.json --baseline eval/latencia-asistente/baseline.json
verification.purpose: one allowed lever, rejected levers with reasons, budget strictly below the baseline p50 and an explicit p95 tolerance

verification.value: read the decision file against the baseline stage table and the bitácora entry
verification.purpose: confirm the choice follows the numbers
verification.expected: the chosen lever targets the stage with the largest measured share

complexity.justification: The prompt asks for three sequential tool rounds while the loop, the sanitising filter and the Python hop each add a different cost, so it is cross-component

scope.justification: The output is one decision entry and a number; nothing in the repository changes

duration.justification: A short ranking and write-up once the table exists, but the table itself is not available to size it against
evidence: assumption:the baseline shows one clearly dominant stage

risk.justification: Choosing the wrong lever wastes the implementation task and risks touching answer quality for no gain

coupling.justification: The decision only reads the T2 output and is ordered after it, with no shared files or resources

confidence.justification: Its content depends on measurements that do not exist, so only the candidate list can be vouched for
evidence: assumption:the measured stage matches one of the candidate levers

tasks.title: Pin the first-turn behaviour with a scripted model
tasks.objective: A no-network test drives the guided turn with a scripted model through the first-turn scenarios and asserts the tool trace, the sanitised reply invariants and the shape of the final fin event, so a latency change that alters behaviour fails
tasks.estimate_rationale: Ordered after the baseline run so the measured server runs the unmodified route. The route imports its chat factory directly and no route-level scripted-model test exists, so a narrow injection seam may be needed first
acceptance_criteria: The test passes against the unmodified behaviour with a scripted model and no network
A scripted turn that skips the brief tool or alters the reply fails the test
The existing guided suite still passes after any seam added to the route

verification.purpose: first-turn tool trace and reply invariants with a scripted model
existing guided suite unchanged by any seam

complexity.justification: A scripted chat port precedent exists for the loop, but wiring it into the route needs a seam that is not yet designed

scope.justification: One new test file plus at most a small injection seam and an npm script entry

duration.justification: The loop test took a third of a second to run, but the route fixtures and the seam make this longer than a plain unit test
evidence: command:npx tsx --test packages/agente-core/test/ejecutar.test.ts -> 4 tests passed in 0.3 s

risk.justification: The seam sits in the production route that shapes customer answers, although the change itself only adds testability

coupling.justification: The route file is later edited by the reduction task and the test is its safety net, and it must not change under the baseline measurement of the previous task

confidence.justification: Whether the route can be driven without changing it was not verified and may force a seam
evidence: assumption:the chat factory can be replaced from a test without editing the route

tasks.title: Apply the chosen latency reduction
tasks.objective: The single lever recorded in the decision file is applied to the first-turn path, with the prompt rules, tools and sanitising that shape the answer functionally intact and the new behaviour covered by tests; the speed-up itself is not claimed here and is measured only by T6
tasks.estimate_rationale: The lever is unknown until T3: it may be a one-line environment default or a change across the round loop, the route and the Python hop; expected_paths is the candidate set of files, not a prediction, and the figure is a placeholder for the middle of that range
acceptance_criteria: The change applies only the lever recorded in the decision file
Whether the budget is met is explicitly left to the T6 measurement and is not asserted at this task
The first-turn test from T4 and the guided suite pass unchanged
The behaviour added or altered by the lever has its own test that fails without it

verification.purpose: guided flows keep behaving the same
first-turn tool trace and reply invariants
TypeScript side of the Python chat hop

complexity.justification: Any candidate lever crosses the route, the round loop or the provider hop, and which one applies is not known yet

scope.justification: Classed large because the candidate levers can span TypeScript and Python layers; the final size depends on the lever

duration.justification: Earlier performance changes in this codebase were commits of a single mechanism each, a useful but loose yardstick

risk.justification: It changes the production path that writes customer-facing answers, and a previous thinking-level change was classed high risk

coupling.justification: The route, the loop and the SSE contract are shared with the pinned test and every guided flow, so edits there interact tightly

confidence.justification: The lever is unknown and the figure is a placeholder, so the estimate cannot be defended any better than this
evidence: assumption:T3 picks one lever that fits one working session

tasks.title: Re-measure and confirm the gain with quality intact
tasks.objective: The file eval/latencia-asistente/after.json is produced by the same harness and scenarios as the baseline and passes budget-check: p50 time to first useful response within the T3 budget and no stage with a worse p95
tasks.estimate_rationale: The run is the same procedure as T2 against the changed code and again needs live paid calls and available quota; whether the budget is met is unknown, the effort of checking is not
acceptance_criteria: The after file uses the same scenarios, run count and flags as the baseline file
The p50 of time to first useful response meets the decision budget
No stage shows a worse p95 than the baseline

verification.value: npx tsx scripts/eval/medir-latencia-asistente.ts budget-check eval/latencia-asistente/after.json --decision eval/latencia-asistente/decision.json --baseline eval/latencia-asistente/baseline.json
verification.purpose: measured p50 within budget, no stage p95 worse, same scenarios and flags
guided flows still pass after the change
Python hop contract holds after the change

complexity.justification: Repeats a procedure already defined and automated by the harness, then compares two tables

scope.justification: Produces a table only and changes no repository file

duration.justification: Same effort as the baseline run, shortened by the harness and the saved scenario list
evidence: command:cd /home/david/dev/pictures/services/ai-api && .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_omoikane_turno_stream.py tests/test_reranker.py -q -> 20 passed in 0.81 s

risk.justification: Only measures and compares; a mistake is caught by reading the two tables side by side

coupling.justification: It reuses the quota and server used by the baseline run and consumes the change from the previous task

confidence.justification: The procedure is known and repeatable, the unknown is the outcome and not the work of checking it
